findings.claim: New CAUTION says the Operator will fail unless the rolling-updates feature is enabled, but the operator never checks the feature; spec.update.strategy is not gated, so the docs are false or the operator gate is missing.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'ROLLING_UPDATES\|rolling-updates' operator/src/main returns nothing; UpgradeLogicFactory.create (UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) switches on spec.update.strategy only; KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:122-124 only passes spec.features through; UpgradeTest's feature enablement would pass identically without it, and upgradeStrategy(null) still expects success.
findings.reason: Three seats independently; grep over operator/src/main is reproducible. Decide: add an operator gate (status error/validation when spec.update set without the feature) or drop the sentence.

findings.claim: The patch renumbers the public exit-code contract (recreate 4->3, feature-disabled=4) but no test asserts either value; swapping them would fail nothing.
findings.evidence: testFeatureNotEnabled checks only error text; testIncompatible checks only error text; the only exit-code assertion in the file is assertEquals(0, ...) at line 75. Tests are @RawDistOnly so result.exitCode() is available. The guide tells users to rely only on the check exit code.
findings.reason: Contract change with zero guard; cheap to add assertEquals(4,...) and assertEquals(3,...). Severity taken from the highest correctness seat (superpowers Important; OCR/mattpocock Minor).

findings.claim: Only the metadata subcommand is run with the feature off; the separate gate copy in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is never exercised.
findings.evidence: The only @Launch without ENABLE_FEATURE is {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME}; UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50 has its own copy of the guard.
findings.reason: One extra @Launch test covers the second copy of the gate; pairs with the exit-code assertion fix.

findings.claim: Exit code 4 is documented as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible', conflating a disabled tool with a compatibility verdict; metadata also returns 4, which the table does not cover.
findings.evidence: UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50 exits with FEATURE_DISABLED; scripts that treat non-zero check as 'recreate' will recreate when the feature is merely off.
findings.reason: Doc-only wording fix; two seats agree and the evidence is a direct code citation.

findings.claim: The feature-disabled guard (isFeatureEnabled / printFeatureDisabled / exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) / return) is duplicated verbatim in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() (both :46-50); printFeatureDisabled() has no other caller.
findings.evidence: grep -rn printFeatureDisabled shows only the definition (AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:83-85) and the two copies; both classes extend AbstractUpdatesCommand.
findings.reason: ponytail: two call sites, behaviour identical, ~5 lines; fold into one AbstractUpdatesCommand helper when a third update subcommand appears.

findings.claim: The macro hard-codes --features=rolling-updates after the user's parameters, overriding features set via KC_FEATURES/keycloak.conf (CLI wins), and a runtime --features on an --optimized image may not take effect since features are build-time.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from option priority and build-time semantics; branch history (b1965bb9c4 'do not use custom image, it fails' then 5d2490d33a baking the feature into Dockerfile-custom-image) points the same way. Not executed.
findings.reason: Unverified, single seat. Settling check: build an image without the feature, then run `kc.sh --optimized update-compatibility metadata --features=rolling-updates --file=x.json` and observe whether it exits 4.

findings.claim: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes 4->3 and 4 is reassigned to feature-disabled; a behaviour change bundled into a feature-flag PR that deserves a release/PR note.
findings.evidence: Base docs table already listed 3 for recreate; command added in 588e60e058 and unreleased (999.0.0-SNAPSHOT).
findings.reason: Both seats' own evidence shows the change aligns code with the base documentation (update-compatibility.adoc already said 3) on an unreleased preview command; no released contract breaks.

findings.claim: Baking --features=rolling-updates into the shared operator test image enables the preview feature for every operator test using the custom image, not just UpgradeTest; not asked for.
findings.evidence: build-testing-docker-images.sh:12 builds one image for the suite; BaseOperatorTest.getTestKeycloakDeployment applies customImage to every deployment.
findings.reason: Intentional per commits b1965bb9c4/5d2490d33a (custom image failed without it); seats report the feature changes no server behaviour beyond the CLI gate, so suite-wide enablement has no observable effect.

findings.claim: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replaces any features the test CR already enabled.
findings.evidence: Raised as a side note by both seats; OCR judged it test-only and harmless today.
findings.reason: Test-only; neither seat counted it as a finding and neither identified a CR in this test that sets features beforehand.

findings.claim: FEATURE_DISABLED drops the _EXIT_CODE suffix used by sibling constants ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE.
findings.reason: Generic naming smell flagged by the seat itself as a judgement call; no documented standard breached.

findings.claim: PR has 5 commits ('feedback', 'fix test failure', ...) and only the first ends with 'Closes #36840'; CONTRIBUTING requires one commit per PR with the issue link last.
findings.evidence: git log 1b28ac610d..HEAD shows c698590195, b1965bb9c4, 5d2490d33a, a44563d5c1, 62bf98939e.
findings.reason: Process, not code; resolved by squash-on-merge, which the seat itself notes.

findings.claim: New preview feature (Profile.java:136) and a CLI behaviour change (update-compatibility now requires --features=rolling-updates) have no release-note entry; PR-CHECKLIST asks for release notes 'if applicable'.
findings.evidence: No hit for rolling-updates under docs/documentation/release_notes.
findings.reason: ponytail: the command is unreleased, so applicability is a maintainer call; add a note when the preview feature ships in a release.

findings.claim: Guide says exit code 1 means missing/corrupt metadata file, but the code throws PropertyException which exits with 2 (usage error).
findings.evidence: Pre-existing on base; reported by the seat as out of scope.
findings.reason: Not touched by this patch; recorded as non-blocking pre-existing issue.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode): no builds, tests or linters executed, so every finding is reasoned, none reproduced by a failing check. Spec axis not run: no spec; mattpocock seat inferred intent from commit messages only and did not fetch issue #36840. Files skipped: none - all four seats report reviewing all 11 patch files; OCR's tool excluded 3 .adoc docs (unsupported_ext) and 2 test files (default_path) but the seat reviewed them by hand. Docs not rendered. Untracked harness dotfiles in the worktree (.bashrc, .claude/, etc.) were excluded from the pinned patch as not part of the PR. Standards docs found: CONTRIBUTING.md, PR-CHECKLIST.md, quarkus/CONTRIBUTING.md. No cross-family reviewer available; all seats same model family, so seat agreement is weak evidence.
